canonical_name: JANUS GATE — PHYSICAL DIORAMA / VIATOR PROTOTYPE
scope: Photographically document the real printed Janus Arch, removable roof Oculus/flywheel, cyan threshold illumination, crossroads floor geometry and human-scale stand-in figure as a spatial demonstrator of the portal architecture.

PORTA.physical_element: four-direction arch body and open passages

LIMEN.physical_element: illuminated central floor/crossroads under the arch

OCULUS.physical_element: nested gyroscopic/fidget rings seated in the roof aperture
OCULUS.role: axis, keystone and visual activation node

LUMEN.physical_element: cyan-blue light entering the cavities from the PC lighting below/inside

VIATOR.physical_element: small armored human figure used as a stand-in traveler
VIATOR.role: demonstrates passage scale, occupancy and human relation to the threshold

canonical_formula: PORTA + LIMEN + OCULUS + LUMEN + VIATOR = PHYSICAL_PORTAL_DIAGRAM
observations: The pale external architecture remains visually distinct from the cyan-lit interior volume.
The roof Oculus reads as a central mechanism rather than as a loose decorative object when viewed from above and from oblique angles.
The illuminated crossroads is centered directly below the roof Oculus, creating a clear vertical axis through the object.
The Viator figure demonstrates that the central volume functions visually as an occupied passage rather than only as an ornamental arch cavity.
Cyan light reflects from the supporting PC surface and visually extends the threshold beyond the printed walls.
The inscription IANUS VIAS SERVAT remains readable on the exterior while the interior presents a contrasting active-state appearance.
From an interior/through-arch viewpoint the Oculus is visible overhead, reinforcing the relation AXIS -> THRESHOLD -> TRAVELER.

photographic_evidence.note: The photographs were used as direct visual evidence for this record. Their SHA-256 fingerprints are recorded below; this JSON does not claim that the image binaries themselves are committed to the repository.

scale_demonstrator_interpretation.claim: The current object is a physical architectural/diorama demonstrator of the Janus Gate composition, not a literal spacetime portal.
validated_by_photos: visual occupancy of the threshold by a traveler stand-in
vertical alignment between roof Oculus and central crossing zone
coherent whole-object reading from front, side, top and interior viewpoints
not_yet_validated: standalone lighting electronics independent of PC illumination

design_implications: Preserve the strong white-stone / cyan-interior contrast in future revisions.
Keep the roof aperture optically open so blue light can illuminate the Oculus from below.
Keep the central crossing visually unobstructed because it is the strongest spatial cue of portal behavior.
Future full-scale lighting should conceal emitters and illuminate surfaces/cavities rather than expose LED hardware.
A future scale prototype should place presence sensors around the four approaches and a token reader outside the threshold, while keeping electronics visually hidden.
The Viator role should remain generic: the system is about passage through a threshold, not identity of a specific traveler.

next_gate.goal: Convert the visual diorama into an instrumented low-energy prototype while preserving the current appearance.
minimum_requirements: add removable hidden controller and power path
add addressable cyan lighting independent of PC RGB
add non-identifying passage sensors for at least two directions
implement DORMANT -> SYNC -> OPEN -> PASSAGE -> REST state machine
document each stage with repeatable tests and hashes

canonical_summary: The printed Janus Arch, cyan internal light, roof-mounted removable Oculus/flywheel, illuminated crossroads and Viator stand-in now form a confirmed physical scale demonstrator of the JANUS GATE architecture. The photographs show a coherent vertical axis from Oculus to central threshold, multiple open routes through PORTA, an active cyan LUMEN field and an occupied LIMEN passage. This record promotes the assembly from a purely visual concept to PHYSICAL_SCALE_DEMONSTRATOR while retaining the explicit boundary that no literal spacetime portal is claimed.
